whatItFakes: A counted adult weighed for a town post is credited with every year since adulthood (appointmentAdulthoodAge) as years of work, because the counts keep no past jobs. It leans toward counted adults: a full person's workYears sums their real spells, so a counted adult with no job now, or with gaps, is credited more than a full person with the same gaps.
why: The counted households keep only the job held now (its kind and how long it has been held), not a work history; filling every candidate in to read one would cost a year's time (gov-appointments-weigh-counted-adults, review of Nov 11).
replacement: The counts keep a work-years figure by age band (from the labor model's own employment rates), read here in place of the years since adulthood.

whatItFakes: In a county whose board hires an administrator who appoints the department heads (research: council-administrator form), the board's seat holder stands in as the appointer of the heads the administrator would pick, so their reasons (loyalty against merit, lean, acquaintance) are the board member's, not the administrator's.
why: The administrator is an appointee, not a seat; the appointment engine's appointer is a seated official (TermRow).
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: The appointer of an administrator-filled post is the person holding the county-administrator appointment, weighed by their own traits.
